# Drizzle ORM Code Generation — Implementation Plan

## Overview

Add a new `drizzle` code generation module to `crates/codegen` that produces TypeScript code for [Drizzle ORM](https://orm.drizzle.team/) from PostgreSQL schema snapshots (`Vec<Table>`). This follows the same architecture as the existing `python` (SQLModel) and `rust` (SeaORM) generators.

### Target Output Example

For a `users` table with `id serial primary key`, `email varchar(255) not null unique`, `name text`, `created_at timestamptz not null`:

```typescript
// Drizzle schema definitions generated by Tern.
//
// This file was automatically generated. Do not edit manually.

import { pgTable, serial, varchar, text, timestamp } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";

export const users = pgTable("users", {
  id: serial("id").primaryKey(),
  email: varchar("email", { length: 255 }).notNull().unique(),
  name: text("name"),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
});
```

For foreign keys and relations (when `generate_relations: true`):

```typescript
import { pgTable, serial, integer, text, timestamp } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { relations } from "drizzle-orm";

export const users = pgTable("users", {
  id: serial("id").primaryKey(),
  name: text("name").notNull(),
});

export const usersRelations = relations(users, ({ many }) => ({
  posts: many(posts),
}));

export const posts = pgTable("posts", {
  id: serial("id").primaryKey(),
  title: text("title").notNull(),
  authorId: integer("author_id").notNull().references(() => users.id),
});

export const postsRelations = relations(posts, ({ one }) => ({
  author: one(users, {
    fields: [posts.authorId],
    references: [users.id],
  }),
}));
```

---

## Module Structure

```
crates/codegen/src/drizzle/
├── mod.rs              # Module root: DrizzleCodegenConfig, OutputMode, error types (mirrors python/mod.rs)
├── generator.rs        # DrizzleCodegen struct implementing Codegen trait (mirrors python/generator.rs)
├── table.rs            # Table definition generation (analogous to python/model.rs)
├── column.rs           # Column builder chain generation (analogous to python/field.rs)
├── type_mapping.rs     # PostgreSQL → Drizzle column builder mapping (mirrors python/type_mapping.rs)
├── naming.rs           # JS/TS identifier sanitization + camelCase conversion (mirrors python/naming.rs)
├── imports.rs          # Import collector for "drizzle-orm/pg-core" etc. (mirrors python/imports.rs)
└── tests/
    ├── unit_tests.rs
    ├── snapshot_tests.rs
    └── snapshots/      # insta snapshot files
```

---

## Detailed Design

### 1. `mod.rs` — Configuration & Error Types

```rust
pub struct DrizzleCodegenConfig {
    /// Output mode: single file or multiple files (one per table).
    pub output_mode: OutputMode,
    /// Whether to generate Drizzle relations (relations() calls).
    pub generate_relations: bool,
    /// Whether to use camelCase for column variable names (with explicit DB column name passed to the builder).
    /// If false, use snake_case matching the DB column name exactly.
    pub camel_case_columns: bool,
    /// Optional schema name (for non-public schemas, uses pgSchema).
    pub schema_name: Option<String>,
}

pub enum OutputMode {
    /// All table definitions in a single `schema.ts` file.
    SingleFile,   // default
    /// Separate files per table, with an `index.ts` barrel export.
    MultiFile,
}

pub enum DrizzleCodegenError {
    UnsupportedType(String),
    EmptyTable(String),
    GenerationError(String),
}
```

**Rationale**: Mirrors `PythonCodegenConfig` structure. `camel_case_columns` defaults to `true` since idiomatic Drizzle uses camelCase JS names with the explicit DB column name string.

### 2. `type_mapping.rs` — PostgreSQL → Drizzle Column Builders

Maps each PG type to a Drizzle column builder function from `drizzle-orm/pg-core`:

| PostgreSQL Type | Drizzle Builder | Import |
|---|---|---|
| `int2`/`smallint` | `smallint` | `smallint` |
| `int4`/`integer` | `integer` | `integer` |
| `int8`/`bigint` | `bigint` | `bigint` |
| `serial`/`serial4` | `serial` | `serial` |
| `bigserial`/`serial8` | `bigserial` | `bigserial` |
| `smallserial`/`serial2` | `smallserial` | `smallserial` |
| `float4`/`real` | `real` | `real` |
| `float8`/`double precision` | `doublePrecision` | `doublePrecision` |
| `numeric`/`decimal` | `numeric` | `numeric` |
| `bool`/`boolean` | `boolean` | `boolean` |
| `text` | `text` | `text` |
| `varchar`/`character varying` | `varchar` | `varchar` |
| `char`/`character`/`bpchar` | `char` | `char` |
| `date` | `date` | `date` |
| `time` | `time` | `time` |
| `timetz` | `time` (with config) | `time` |
| `timestamp` | `timestamp` | `timestamp` |
| `timestamptz` | `timestamp` (with `{ withTimezone: true }`) | `timestamp` |
| `interval` | `interval` | `interval` |
| `uuid` | `uuid` | `uuid` |
| `json` | `json` | `json` |
| `jsonb` | `jsonb` | `jsonb` |
| `bytea` | `customType(...)` or `text` | (varies) |
| `inet`/`cidr`/`macaddr` | `inet`/`cidr`/`macaddr` | same |
| `point`/`line`/etc. | `customType(...)` or fallback | (varies) |
| arrays | Drizzle doesn't have first-class array support; will emit a warning comment | — |
| unknown/enum types | `text` with a warning comment, or `pgEnum` if enum definitions are available | `pgEnum` |

The return type:

```rust
pub struct DrizzleColumnType {
    /// The builder function name (e.g., "serial", "varchar", "timestamp").
    pub builder: String,
    /// Additional config object for the builder (e.g., `{ length: 255 }`, `{ withTimezone: true }`).
    pub config: Option<String>,
    /// Required import names from "drizzle-orm/pg-core".
    pub imports: Vec<String>,
    /// Warning if this type mapping is approximate.
    pub warning: Option<String>,
}
```

### 3. `column.rs` — Column Builder Chain

Generates the chained method call for each column. For a column like `email varchar(255) not null unique`, produces:

```
varchar("email", { length: 255 }).notNull().unique()
```

Logic:
1. Start with the builder function + column name argument + optional config from type_mapping
2. Append `.primaryKey()` if the column is the sole PK column
3. Append `.notNull()` if `!is_nullable` (and not a serial/identity PK, which is implicitly not null)
4. Append `.unique()` if column has a single-column unique constraint
5. Append `.default(...)` if column has a default value expression
6. Append `.references(() => otherTable.column)` if column has a single-column FK

```rust
pub struct ColumnInfo {
    /// The JS variable name for the column (camelCase or snake_case).
    pub js_name: String,
    /// The original DB column name.
    pub db_name: String,
    /// The complete builder chain expression.
    pub builder_chain: String,
    /// Required imports.
    pub imports: Vec<String>,
    /// Warnings for this column.
    pub warnings: Vec<String>,
}
```

### 4. `table.rs` — Table Definition Generation

Generates the `pgTable(...)` call for a table. For composite primary keys and composite unique constraints, uses the third argument to `pgTable`:

```typescript
export const orderItems = pgTable("order_items", {
  orderId: integer("order_id").notNull(),
  productId: integer("product_id").notNull(),
  quantity: integer("quantity").notNull(),
}, (table) => [
  primaryKey({ columns: [table.orderId, table.productId] }),
  unique("order_items_order_product").on(table.orderId, table.productId),
]);
```

```rust
pub struct TableInfo {
    /// The JS variable name for the table (camelCase plural, e.g., `users`).
    pub js_name: String,
    /// The DB table name.
    pub db_name: String,
    /// Column definitions.
    pub columns: Vec<ColumnInfo>,
    /// Extra constraints (composite PK, composite unique, check, indexes).
    pub extra_constraints: Vec<String>,
    /// Required imports from "drizzle-orm/pg-core".
    pub imports: Vec<String>,
    /// Warnings.
    pub warnings: Vec<String>,
    /// Relations code (if generate_relations is enabled).
    pub relations: Option<String>,
}
```

### 5. `naming.rs` — JS/TS Identifier Handling

- `to_table_variable_name(table_name: &str) -> String`: Table names stay as-is in snake_case (Drizzle convention uses the DB name as the JS variable, e.g., `export const users = ...`). No singularization.
- `to_column_name(column_name: &str, camel_case: bool) -> (String, bool)`: If `camel_case`, convert `user_id` → `userId`. Returns `(js_name, needs_explicit_db_name)`.
- `sanitize_js_identifier(name: &str) -> (String, bool)`: Handle JS reserved words (`class`, `default`, `delete`, `export`, `import`, `new`, `return`, `switch`, `this`, `typeof`, etc.) by appending underscore.
- `to_relation_name(table_name: &str, column_name: &str) -> String`: Generate relation field names (e.g., FK `author_id` → relation name `author`).

### 6. `imports.rs` — Import Management

Simpler than Python since all column builders come from a single module:

```rust
pub struct ImportCollector {
    /// Imports from "drizzle-orm/pg-core" (pgTable, serial, text, etc.)
    pg_core: BTreeSet<String>,
    /// Imports from "drizzle-orm" (relations, etc.)
    drizzle_orm: BTreeSet<String>,
    /// Cross-table imports for references (in multi-file mode)
    table_imports: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
}
```

Output:
```typescript
import { pgTable, serial, text, varchar, timestamp } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { relations } from "drizzle-orm";
```

### 7. `generator.rs` — DrizzleCodegen

Implements `Codegen` trait:

- **SingleFile mode**: Produces `schema.ts` with all tables and relations
- **MultiFile mode**: Produces one `<table_name>.ts` per table + `index.ts` barrel export

```rust
pub struct DrizzleCodegen {
    config: DrizzleCodegenConfig,
}

impl Codegen for DrizzleCodegen {
    fn generate(&self, tables: Vec<Table>) -> HashMap<String, String> { ... }
}
```

### 8. `lib.rs` Changes

Add `pub mod drizzle;` to `crates/codegen/src/lib.rs`.

### 9. Note on `genco`

The `genco` crate (v0.19.0, already a dependency) supports JavaScript via `genco::lang::JavaScript`. However, the existing Python and Rust generators in this codebase do **not** use genco — they use manual string building. For consistency with the existing codebase, this implementation will also use manual string building. Genco could be adopted later as a refactor across all three generators.

---

## Test Plan

### Unit Tests (`tests/unit_tests.rs`)

1. **Type mapping**: Verify each PG type maps to the correct Drizzle builder + config
2. **Column generation**: Test builder chains for PK, FK, nullable, unique, default, varchar length
3. **Naming**: camelCase conversion, JS reserved word handling, table variable names
4. **Table generation**: Single table, composite PK, composite unique constraints
5. **Import collection**: Correct deduplication and ordering
6. **Relations**: One-to-many, many-to-one relation generation
7. **Config options**: camelCase vs snake_case, with/without relations

### Snapshot Tests (`tests/snapshot_tests.rs`)

Using `insta` (already a dev-dependency):

1. **Simple users table** — single PK, varchar, text, timestamp columns
2. **Blog schema** — users + posts + comments with FK relations
3. **Complex types** — all supported PG types in one table
4. **Composite primary key** — table with multi-column PK
5. **Multi-file output** — verify per-table files + index.ts
6. **Reserved words** — table/columns using JS reserved words
7. **Non-public schema** — using `pgSchema`
8. **Self-referential FK** — table referencing itself

---

## Implementation Order

1. `type_mapping.rs` — PG to Drizzle type mapping (standalone, easily testable)
2. `naming.rs` — identifier conversion (standalone)
3. `imports.rs` — import collector (standalone)
4. `column.rs` — column builder chain (depends on type_mapping, naming)
5. `table.rs` — table definition generation (depends on column, imports)
6. `mod.rs` — config types and error types
7. `generator.rs` — Codegen trait implementation (depends on table, imports)
8. `lib.rs` — wire up `pub mod drizzle`
9. Tests — unit tests and snapshot tests
10. `cargo make format` + `cargo make clippy` — mandatory checks
